Rows read on page images (no quotation, the transcription between « and » in the note): the figures of Phillips's curve, his Table 1 and his conclusions (pp. 290, 298, 299), where the text layer misreads them; Okun (1962) and Klein (1950, including the preface, pp. vii-viii), whose scans have no text layer; the President's signature in the Economic Report of 1962. Misreadings of the text layers and misprints, each as printed in the quotation: 'accura ely' for 'accurately' (ph_predict); '2~' for 2½ (ph_stable_text); '51' for 5½ (ph_wages5_text); '9*638' and '1394' for 9·638 and 1·394 (ph_curve_text); 'Iate' for 'rate' (ph_example); 'decisionl' for 'decision' (ph_gold); 'tbp' for 'the' (ph_1948src); 'betwveen' for 'between' (ph_1922b); 'Tcchnology' for 'Technology' (ss_mit); 'miobility' for 'mobility' (ss_mobility); '2Y2' for 2½ (ss_phillips5); "2'2" for 2½ (ss_point1); '512' for 5½ (ss_pointA); '412' for 4½ (ss_pointB); '1958' for 1968 (e71_c45_1968); '1989' for 1969 (e71_c45_1969); 'B.C.' for 'D.C.' (erp_transmitted); 'Tinbergen 's' with a space (nbb_reviving). Decimal points the text layer of Phillips (1958) loses or reads as '*' or '-', read by the rule 'ocr' of checks/check_ch38.py (the page images agree): '12*5' (ph_1862), '2 8', '3 -6' and '2 -7' (ph_1912), '0 8' (ph_1912adj), '2 6', '17 0' and '22 2' (ph_1921), '12 8' (ph_1921b), '14*3' and '19*1' (ph_1922), '17 *5' (ph_1922b), '9 7' and '12- 5' (ph_1925), '10 94' and '- 0 *60' (ph_1925avg), '- 0*56' (ph_1925curve). Disagreements between the sources: Samuelson and Solow say that Phillips's money wages stabilize at 5 per cent unemployment and that 2-3 per cent productivity growth goes with about 2½ per cent unemployment (ss_phillips5); Phillips writes about 5½ per cent (ph_wages5) and 2 per cent productivity growth with a little under 2½ per cent (ph_stable). The press release of 1980 calls the prize one 'for the creation of economic models' (nb_citation), the facts page 'for the creation of econometric models' (nbf_motivation). The press release and the facts page call Klein's study of 1950 'a paper' (nb_paper1950, nbf_paper1950); it is the monograph of the Cowles Commission (kl_cfm, kl_title). Fisher (1926) states his 90 per cent as a correlation between the rate of change in the value of the dollar and unemployment (fi_90); the correlation he computes is between price change, spread by the distributed lag, and the Harvard Committee's index of employment, which combines statistics of employment and unemployment (fi_pe, fi_e, fi_e_fn). Canada's unemployment rate of 1961: 7.1 per cent in Historical Statistics of Canada (hs_d491_1961), 7.2 per cent in Powell (Chapter 37, mundell_facts). The series of the book's recomputation (boe_millennium_uk_1860_1958) are Feinstein's average weekly earnings and, from 1920, his unemployment as a percentage of the civilian working population; Phillips used the hourly wage index of Phelps Brown and Hopkins (ph_pbh), the Ministry of Labour's indexes (ph_1921src, ph_1948wage) and the Ministry's unemployment percentages for Great Britain (ph_1948src). Single witnesses: Phillips's curve, crosses and Table 1 (ph_curve, ph_fit, ph_t1_1948 to ph_t1_1957); Samuelson and Solow's points A and B (ss_pointA, ss_pointB); Okun's coefficient (ok_weighted, ok_rule); the gap and the labour force of 1961 (erp_gap49, erp_gap50, erp_jobs); Klein's estimates (kl_est_c, kl_est_i, kl_est_w); Okun's year of death (loc_okun_note). Indirect testimony: Friedman quoting Keynes's 'one equation' (fr_gap); Samuelson and Solow on Hume (ss_hume) and on Phillips (ss_phillips5); Klein's career in his autobiography (nbb_samuelson, nbb_reviving, nbb_ottawa, nbb_goldberger) and in the press release (nb_tinbergen, nb_aim, nb_famous, nb_forecasts). Not obtained: Lipsey (1960) (only Phillips's thanks to R. G. Lipsey: ph_ack); Klein and Goldberger, An Econometric Model of the United States, 1929-1952 (the Internet Archive has only a lending copy, of a printing of 1964: ar_kg, ar_kg_lending); Keynes's review of Tinbergen (1939) and Tinbergen's reply; Haavelmo (1944); Modigliani (1944); Adelman and Adelman (1959); the reprint of Fisher (1926) in the Journal of Political Economy (1973); Forder (2014); the date on which Samuelson and Solow read their paper (the American Economic Association's pages did not open); the House of Commons debates (the Hansard website refused access). Life dates: Phillips, Samuelson, Klein, Tinbergen, Fisher, Hume, Kennedy, Friedman and Keynes from the Library of Congress; Phillips, Samuelson and Klein also from the GND, which agrees; Solow, Goldberger and Coyne from the GND (the LoC heading of Solow has no years, that of Goldberger no year of death: loc_solow, loc_goldberger); Okun: the LoC heading has no years (loc_okun); the record's source note, citing Who Was Who in America, vol. 7 ('WwasW, v. 7'), gives born 28 November 1928 and died 23 May 1980 (loc_okun_note, loc_okun_source); the GND and the BnF give 1928 and no year of death (gnd_okun_born, bnf_okun), which agrees. Klein's dates also on the Nobel pages (nbf_born, nbb_died).
